title: Cyber Monday 2026 — US e-commerce peak day (collides with AWS re:Invent day 1)
source: EST: derived by statute and weekday arithmetic, corroborated inside this repo and against three independent aggregators. Cyber Monday is by universal trade convention the Monday after Thanksgiving; Thanksgiving is the FOURTH THURSDAY of November (5 U.S.C. 6103). November 2026 opens on a Sunday, so its Thursdays are the 5th, 12th, 19th and 26th — the fourth is 2026-11-26 and the Monday after it is 2026-11-30. The tracked entries thanksgiving-market-closure-2026-11-26 and thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27 corroborate that anchor from inside this repo without circularity (a full closure on the Thursday and a 13:00 ET early close on the Friday only exist if Thanksgiving is 2026-11-26). Secondary corroboration NEWS: awarenessdays.com, calendardate.com and wikidates.org all list Cyber Monday 2026 as Monday 30 November 2026 (searched 2026-09-09). ONE AGGREGATOR DISSENTS AND IS WRONG: a nationaldaycalendar.com search-result title reads 'CYBER MONDAY - December 1, 2026'; 2026-12-01 is a TUESDAY, which the site's own stated rule (the Monday after Thanksgiving) cannot produce, and a direct fetch of the page returned HTTP 403 so the discrepancy could not be run down at source (recorded in the ledger's probe-ref.blocked). Filed estimate on three counts, none of which is doubt about the date: no IR:/CENSUS:-class primary publishes a 'Cyber Monday' date because it is a marketing convention rather than a scheduled release; the datable ARTIFACT is Adobe Analytics' recap, whose publication time is a vendor decision with no published calendar and has moved a full trading session between consecutive years (2024-12-03 09:00 ET pre-market vs 2025-12-02 17:00 ET post-close); and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Discovered 2026-09-09 by the aws-reinvent-2026 lane; canonical file written 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research
notes: CANONICAL FILE, written from proposals/cyber-monday-2026-11-30.from-aws-reinvent-2026.json (the only proposal for this id), which is now inert and stays where it is. The proposer's finding stands: 2026-11-30 is AWS re:Invent day 1 (confirmed, IR: aws.amazon.com/events/reinvent) AND AMZN's largest retail day, so AMZN is the only symbol in this calendar whose cloud and retail narratives land a headline on one session. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE PROPOSAL, both verified 2026-09-09: (1) the '$250B+/+5.3% y/y' figure it attributed to a 2026 season forecast is Adobe's 2025-SEASON forecast ($253.4B, +5.3% y/y for Nov 1 - Dec 31 2025, published 2025-10-06 via retaildive.com); the 2025 season actually printed $257.8B (+6.8%), and Adobe has NOT published a 2026-season forecast as of 2026-09-09. (2) the recap does not reliably land 'the following morning' — Adobe's Cyber Monday 2025 recap published 2025-12-02 at 17:00 ET (AFTER the cash close, so a CM+2 input) while the 2024 recap published 2024-12-03 at 09:00 ET (pre-market, a CM+1 input). WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH MEASURED (docs/research/events/cyber-monday-2026-11-30.md): 26 Cyber Mondays, split/dividend-adjusted daily closes. AMZN has NO usable edge on the session (2013+: AMZN-SPY mean +0.31pp, 7/13 up) and the recap session is a coin flip (AMZN-SPY 11/26 up, binomial p=0.56). What survives is a RELATIVE-VALUE spread, not a directional call: AMZN minus XRT on the Cyber Monday session runs +1.35pp mean, 16/20 up, t=3.40 (beta-adjusted residual +1.34pp, t=3.27), against an AMZN-XRT daily base rate of 50.7% up / +0.076pp, with both placebos flat (all Mondays 47.1% up; the Monday five sessions earlier 9/20). Registered as FT-cyber-monday-2026-11-30-1, NOT deployed — it needs a short leg and shorting is blocked in this book (multi-symbol-sweep.md), and its raw p=0.012 does not clear this house's ~0.001 family-corrected bar after ~12 tests. XRT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN `symbols`: that field is the tracked-name roster (AAPL AMZN AVGO CRWV GOOG META MRVL MSFT, no ETFs), and widening the calendar's symbol vocabulary is a calendar-wide decision, not a research lane's to take unilaterally. CONSIDERED AND DECLINED as adjacency proposals so the absences read as decisions: Black Friday 2026-11-27 (already tracked as thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27; a second entry double-counts one shortened session); Adobe's 2026-season holiday forecast (cadence points at early October 2026 off the 2025-10-06 precedent, but no primary pins a date); the Adobe Cyber Monday 2026 recap itself (it is the MEASUREMENT of this event, not a separate event, and its time-of-day is unstable); the Census Q4-2026 quarterly e-commerce release (its scheduled-release PDF would not parse and no primary date could be read); and Green Monday 2026-12-14 (a marketing convention with no measured reaction function here). NAMED LIMIT: a convention is not a scheduled release, and an estimate-labelled date may only widen caution - nothing here licenses an entry. S1 is killed on AMZN (p=0.6854).
